chosen_format.why_it_works: escalating negation list builds rhythm and each 'no' raises the stakes. the vulgar verb phrase before the payoff is what makes it shareable. subject is admired for refusing the easy path, so the product reads as the sane option without being pitched
chosen_format.text_skeleton: my {RELATION} {DOING_THE_THING} after {LIFE_DECISION}. no {ALT_1}. no {ALT_2}. no {ALT_3}. no {COMPETITOR}. just {PRONOUN} and {LAST_RESORT_TOOL}. {VULGAR_VERB_PHRASE} like a psychopath
chosen_format.visual_mechanic: dead-pan stare into camera, single slow nod on the last line

format_scores.reason: The 'no Jira, no Asana, no Notion' escalating negation list maps cleanly onto the named competitors and the 'just them and Linear' payoff frames the product as the sane-but-admired choice, though the 'psychopath' admiration framing slightly undercuts Linear's sharp, no-nonsense tone by making the user seem reckless rather than disciplined.

The self-check list mechanic maps well onto Linear's core pain—engineers can tick off each Jira-style dysfunction (manual ticket copying, buried backlogs, no shipping velocity) as a red flag in a project management tool, making the brand's green flag payoff feel earned rather than pitched, though the dating-language framing is a mild tonal stretch for Linear's sharp, no-nonsense voice.

The 'delusional confidence gap' mechanic maps well to Linear's core pain because the joke writes itself — claiming you'll ship a product in a week while you're still manually copying Slack messages into Jira is exactly the absurd disconnect the format needs, and the reveal (Linear's AI handling the grunt work) lands in the same beat as the brand mention, hitting the_hard_way directly.

The 'unglamorous discipline habit list' mechanic fits the brand's no-nonsense tone and could naturally slot Linear usage alongside mundane dev rituals (standups, PR reviews), but it doesn't directly target the core pain of being buried in tickets or the specific hard way of copying Slack messages into Jira—the self-deprecating reframe works generically but doesn't sharpen against Linear's particular enemy.
